why: This is the sliding-window-log rate limiter: each client keeps a deque of its accepted timestamps, old ones fall out the front when they are at most t - windowSeconds, and a request is accepted while the deque holds fewer than maxRequests entries. A hash map from client id to deque keeps clients independent.
hints: Each client is independent, and only that client's accepted requests matter. What do you need to remember per client?
Keep a queue of accepted timestamps per client. Because timestamps arrive in order, expired entries are always at the front.
Map clientId -> deque. For each request: pop from the front while dq[0] <= t - windowSeconds, then accept and append t if len(dq) < maxRequests. Amortised O(1) per request.
pitfalls: Expiry boundary is inclusive: a request at exactly t - windowSeconds has left the window (example 2 at time 3 with window 3).
Rejected requests are not recorded and do not use capacity.
Requests with equal timestamps are handled one by one in input order.
